text: The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris, France, on the Champ de Mars near the Seine river. It was designed by Gustave Eiffel's engineering company and completed in 1889 as the entrance arch for that year's World's Fair. It stands about 330 metres tall including its antennas.

The Great Wall of China is not visible to the naked eye from space, including from low Earth orbit, according to multiple astronauts including China's own Yang Liwei. It is long but very narrow, and its color blends with the surrounding terrain. It can, however, be photographed from orbit with a telephoto lens.

Honey can remain edible for decades or even centuries if stored in a sealed container, thanks to its low moisture content and acidity, which prevent bacterial growth. Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were still chemically intact.

Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius (212 degrees Fahrenheit) at standard atmospheric pressure (sea level). The boiling point drops at higher altitudes because atmospheric pressure is lower; on top of Mount Everest, water boils at around 70 degrees Celsius.

Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and Tibet, has a peak at 8,849 metres above sea level, making it the highest point above sea level on Earth. Measured from base to peak, Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller overall, but most of it lies underwater.
An adult human skeleton has 206 bones. Babies are born with roughly 270 to 300 bones, many of which are cartilage that fuses together into fewer, larger bones during childhood and adolescence.

The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792 kilometres per second (about 186,282 miles per second). This value, denoted c, is a fundamental physical constant and is treated as an absolute speed limit for information and matter in current physics.

Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969, with Armstrong becoming the first human to step onto the lunar surface. Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard the command module.

The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceans, covering roughly one third of the planet's surface — more area than all of Earth's land combined. It stretches from the Arctic in the north to the Southern Ocean near Antarctica.

The Nile is traditionally cited as the world's longest river at roughly 6,650 kilometres, flowing through northeastern Africa. Some studies using different measurement methods argue the Amazon River in South America is actually longer, so the title is genuinely contested among geographers rather than settled.

James Watson and Francis Crick published the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953, building heavily on X-ray diffraction images captured by Rosalind Franklin and data from Maurice Wilkins. Franklin's contribution was not widely publicly credited during her lifetime.

The Great Barrier Reef off the coast of Queensland, Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 kilometres and composed of roughly 2,900 individual reefs. It is large enough to be seen from space.

The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, covering most of North Africa. However, Antarctica and the Arctic are technically the largest deserts overall, since a desert is defined by low precipitation rather than temperature.

Most geographers and atlases recognise seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia (Oceania), Europe, North America, and South America. Some models used in parts of Europe and Latin America combine these into five or six continents, so the count is a convention rather than a fixed physical fact.

Napoleon Bonaparte was approximately 5 feet 7 inches (about 170 centimetres) tall in modern measurements, close to the average height for a Frenchman of his era. The 'short Napoleon' myth largely stems from a mix-up between French and British measurement units at the time, and from British wartime propaganda cartoons.

Goldfish do not have a three-second memory. Multiple studies have shown goldfish can remember and respond to learned cues, sounds, and routines for weeks or even months, and can be trained to navigate mazes and recognise feeding schedules.

Lightning frequently strikes the same location more than once. Tall, exposed structures are struck repeatedly; the Empire State Building in New York is struck by lightning roughly 20 to 25 times per year on average.

Bats are not blind. Most bat species have functional eyes and can see, some quite well in low light; they additionally use echolocation to navigate and hunt in complete darkness, which is a separate sense rather than a replacement for sight.

Venus, not Mercury, is the hottest planet in our solar system, with average surface temperatures around 465 degrees Celsius. Despite Mercury being closer to the Sun, Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat through an intense greenhouse effect.

Russia is the largest country in the world by total land area, spanning eleven time zones across Europe and Asia. Canada is second largest, followed by the United States and China, though the exact ranking of the third and fourth spots depends on how disputed territories and water area are counted.
